definitions.gloss: counter word, counter suffix, numerical classifier
definitions.explanation: A grammatical term for the suffixes attached to numbers when counting things in Japanese. Different counters are used depending on what is being counted — flat things, long things, people, animals, etc. Also called {数|かぞ}え{方|かた} informally.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}には{多|おお}くの{助数詞|じょすうし}がある。
{助数詞|じょすうし}の{使|つか}い{方|かた}は{外国人|がいこくじん}にとって{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: The use of counter words is difficult for foreigners.

examples.japanese: {正|ただ}しい{助数詞|じょすうし}を{使|つか}えるようになると、{日本語|にほんご}がより{自然|しぜん}に{聞|き}こえる。
examples.english: When you can use the correct counter words, your Japanese will sound more natural.

notes:
A linguistic term that learners of Japanese encounter frequently. Common counters include {枚|まい} (flat things), {本|ほん} (long things), {匹|ひき} (small animals), {冊|さつ} (books), {台|だい} (machines/vehicles), and {杯|はい} (cups/glasses). Knowing which counter to use with which object is one of the distinctive challenges of Japanese.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {助数詞|じょすうし}を{使|つか}う (to use a counter word)
- {助数詞|じょすうし}を{覚|おぼ}える (to learn counter words)
- {助数詞|じょすうし}の{一覧|いちらん} (list of counter words)
